about: build.header_patches rule `vector-destruct-end-first`: std::vector's __base_destruct_at_end (clear, a resize or
erase that shrinks it, the destructor) loops `while (__soon_to_be_end != __new_last)`, the moving end on the
left, where libc++'s releases 16 to 22 write `while (__new_last != __soon_to_be_end)`. clang keeps the operands'
order in the loop's compare (`cmp end, new_last` against `cmp new_last, end`), so every vector of elements with
a destructor compiles otherwise. zkit edits a copy of the release's header whose SHA-256 is the patch's `sha256`
